name: Differentiable Forward Warping with Average Splatting
definition: A warping strategy that estimates deformation from canonical time to another time step, ensuring smooth flows. It uses average splatting to handle the many-to-one issue where multiple source positions map to one target position.
summary: Differentiable Forward Warping with Average Splatting synthesizes dynamic scenes by warping canonical volumetric representations using estimated deformation flows and fusing multiple source contributions via weighted averaging to resolve many-to-one mapping conflicts.
